name: Martin Hannett
hook: Isolated the drums, gated the reverb, and made a Manchester punk band's aftermath sound like it was recorded in an empty warehouse at 3am.

blurb.age7: Martin Hannett was the producer who made Joy Division's music sound cold and spacious, with lots of echo.
blurb.age13: Hannett produced Joy Division's two albums, 'Unknown Pleasures' (1979) and 'Closer' (1980), using unusual techniques for the time, isolating and gating the drums, layering artificial reverb and echo, to build a sound far starker than the band's live performances. He was also closely tied to Factory Records, the Manchester label that released both albums.
blurb.adult: Hannett's studio techniques are frequently credited with defining Joy Division's recorded sound as much as the band's own songwriting did, a genuinely contested claim among the surviving members themselves, some of whom have said the records sound more like Hannett's vision than their live sets did at the time.

signatureTracks.title: Unknown Pleasures (produced for Joy Division)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The debut album where Hannett's spacious, gated production first defined the band's recorded identity.

signatureTracks.title: Closer (produced for Joy Division)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Released weeks after Ian Curtis's death, and the fuller realization of Hannett's cold, echo-heavy approach.
